trip-fields-corner.text:
I am an independent prototype, not a City of Boston or MBTA service.

Planned as the showcase trip "Fields Corner, Dorchester to Downtown Crossing" at its fixed demo departure, Tuesday 08:15. Both places resolved cleanly (Fields Corner and Downtown Crossing stations). The alert source in use is `none` — it returned no alerts — so disruption risk is 0 on every route and nothing is synthetic or rerouted. Crash risk is an estimated index (Boston Vision Zero + Cambridge police crash counts per estimated peak-hour volume) covering walking and biking segments only; driving and transit vehicle crash risk is not modeled. CO2 is estimated from emission_factors.yaml (EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub 2025 for drive/subway; zero operational emissions for walk/bike).

Fastest is the drive at ~9.9 min (free-flow, ignores traffic), 1,444 g CO2 estimated. Every other route's trade-off is against that:

- **Red Line (transit):** ~22.7 min, 411 g CO2 estimated, crash risk index 3.5. Trade-off: 12.9 min slower, ~72% less CO2. Part of its crash risk uses a road-class estimate because no count data covers those streets.
- **Bike, safer variant 3:** ~38.6 min, 0 g CO2 estimated, crash risk index 1,098. Trade-off: 28.7 min slower, 100% less CO2. Part of its crash risk is a road-class estimate (no counts on those streets).
- **Bike, safer variant 2:** ~35.3 min, 0 g CO2 estimated, crash risk index 1,243. Trade-off: 25.4 min slower, 100% less CO2. A small part of its crash risk is a road-class estimate.
- **Bike, safer variant 1:** ~34.6 min, 0 g CO2 estimated, crash risk index 1,315. Trade-off: 24.7 min slower, 100% less CO2. A small part of its crash risk is a road-class estimate.
- **Walk, safer variant 1:** ~99.2 min, 0 g CO2 estimated, crash risk index 55.8. Trade-off: 89.3 min slower, 100% less CO2. All of its crash risk uses a road-class estimate.
- **Walk, safer variant 2:** ~100.6 min, 0 g CO2 estimated, crash risk index 51.4. Trade-off: 90.8 min slower, 100% less CO2. All of its crash risk uses a road-class estimate.
- **Walk, fastest:** ~96.1 min, 0 g CO2 estimated, crash risk index 353. Trade-off: 86.2 min slower, 100% less CO2 — but roughly six times the crash-risk index of the safer walk variants. All of its crash risk uses a road-class estimate.
- **Walk, safer variant 3:** ~108.1 min, 0 g CO2 estimated, crash risk index 44.5 (lowest crash risk in the plan). Trade-off: 98.2 min slower, 100% less CO2. All of its crash risk uses a road-class estimate.
- **Drive:** ~9.9 min, 1,444 g CO2 estimated, crash risk not modeled — this is the fastest and least disrupted route, but its time is free-flow and ignores traffic.
- **Bike, fastest:** ~33.0 min, 0 g CO2 estimated (also tagged lowest CO2), crash risk index 2,851 — the highest crash risk in the plan. Trade-off: 23.1 min slower, 100% less CO2. A very small part of its crash risk is a road-class estimate. Bluebikes dock availability was not checked.

Short version: the Red Line is only ~13 min behind driving with ~72% less CO2 and near-zero crash-risk index; among the bike options the safer variants cut the risk index roughly in half versus the fastest bike route at a cost of a few minutes.

Tell me which one you'll take and I'll record it.

trip-maverick.text:
I am an independent prototype, not a City of Boston or MBTA service.

Both places resolved: Maverick Square, East Boston → Courthouse. This plan used the departure **2026-10-27 08:15** — it's a showcase trip planned at its fixed demo departure. The alert source was none, so no disruption is priced in.

The fastest route is **Drive** (5.46 min, est. 874 g CO2), so the trade-offs below are against it.

- **Blue Line** (listed first, 20.03 min): 14.57 min slower than driving, 89.91% less CO2 (estimated, EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub 2025 for rail). Crash risk is an estimated index for walking/biking segments only, from Boston Vision Zero and Cambridge police counts; driving and transit vehicle crash risk is not modeled. Its unknown_exposure_share is 1.0, so its crash risk uses a road-class estimate because no count data covers those streets.
- **Blue Line, then 4** (16.83 min): 11.37 min slower, 79.75% less CO2 (estimated, EPA factors for rail and bus). Walking-only crash index; unknown_exposure_share 1.0 (road-class estimate); no transit vehicle crash risk modeled.
- **Walk, safer variant 1** (138.75 min): 133.29 min slower, 100% less CO2. Labelled lowest crash risk, an estimated index from Vision Zero/Cambridge counts per estimated peak-hour volume; unknown_exposure_share 1.0 (road-class estimate).
- **Drive** (5.46 min, fastest and least disrupted): est. 874 g CO2 (EPA Hub 2025, US average; free-flow time ignoring traffic). A crash risk of 0 means it is not modeled, not that it is safe.
- **Walk, fastest** (137.23 min): 131.76 min slower, 100% less CO2; higher estimated crash index than the safer walk variant; unknown_exposure_share 1.0.
- **Bike, safer variant 1** (46.51 min): 41.04 min slower, 100% less CO2; estimated crash index for bike segments (Vision Zero/Cambridge counts), with unknown_exposure_share 0.41 (part road-class estimate) plus Bluebikes-proxy coverage. Bluebikes dock availability is not checked.
- **Bike, safer variant 3** (55.12 min): 49.66 min slower, 100% less CO2; estimated crash index with unknown_exposure_share 0.55 — the lowest estimated crash index of the bike routes.
- **Bike, fastest** (45.93 min): 40.47 min slower, 100% less CO2; the highest estimated crash index shown, unknown_exposure_share 0.42.

Suggestion: the **Blue Line on its own** is the simplest low-carbon option (est. 88 g CO2); **Blue Line then 4** is quicker at 16.83 min but its est. CO2 is 177 g.
